# MacOSCleaner — full brief for AI agents

> Free source-available macOS cleaner & app uninstaller for Apple Silicon. Offline. No telemetry. Personal use only.

## What it is

Native SwiftUI utility that helps reclaim disk space and uninstall apps cleanly on Apple Silicon Macs. Scanning and cleanup stay on-device. No account, no cloud upload, no telemetry/analytics pipeline.

It complements (does not replace) Apple’s built-in storage recommendations. Apple’s tools are strong for large personal files; MacOSCleaner goes deeper on caches, developer artifacts, and incomplete uninstall leftovers.

## Core features

1. Smart Cleanup — 54 categories, 450+ built-in paths; parallel scan; risk badges (Safe / Moderate / Dangerous / Protected); user confirms before delete. Permanent delete is opt-in; many flows prefer Trash.
2. App Uninstaller — drag-and-drop `.app`; forensic leftover scan up to 5 levels; ~30 evidence types (Bundle ID, Team ID, Spotlight, plist, Launch Services); confidence tiers; Safe or Balanced mode.
3. Disk Space Analyzer — scan any folder; sort by size; filter Video / Audio / Photos / Apps / Documents / Archives; Reveal in Finder or Trash; background scanning.
4. Process Manager — flat/grouped views; sort by CPU/Memory/Name/Threads; whitelist/blacklist; system processes protected.
5. Startup Services — LaunchAgents / LaunchDaemons from `~/Library` and `/Library`; group User / Third-party / System; load, unload, stop (admin prompt when needed).
6. Apple Intelligence (on supported hardware) — on-device `FoundationModels` explanations for files, caches, processes, startup agents; offline; output EN / RU / UK / ES.
7. Liquid Glass UI on macOS 27+ — native glass materials; respects Reduce Transparency.
8. Localized UI — English, Русский, Українська, Español.
9. Smart Updates — checks GitHub Releases on launch; no background daemon required for everyday use.

## Typical cleanup targets

- App & browser caches (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, Arc, messengers, IDEs, etc.)
- Package managers: Homebrew, npm, yarn, pnpm, CocoaPods
- Dev tools: Xcode DerivedData / simulators, Android SDK, Gradle/Maven, Flutter/Dart, Go, Rust, Python, Node, Swift PM, Bazel
- IDE & AI tool caches: Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Zed, JetBrains, Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, etc.
- System & Docker-related data (prune where safe), crash reports, large installers (DMG/pkg/iso), orphans in HTTPStorages / WebKit / Cookies, `node_modules`, iPhone backups, IPSW
- Opt-in toggles for sensitive large paths (e.g. Maven `~/.m2`, Go mod cache, Flutter `.dart_tool`, some media/iCloud areas)

## Safety model

- Review-first workflow: Scan → Review → Clean → Verify
- Uninstaller and Disk Analyzer use Trash (`trashItem(at:)`) by default
- `SafetyManager` blocks critical paths (`/System`, `/usr`, `~/.ssh`, and similar)
- Does not wipe user source repositories for Xcode/Docker cleanup — targets known cache/tooling paths; user must still review results
- Logs: Console.app, subsystem `input.MacOSCleaner`

## Privacy

- No telemetry, no analytics, nothing sent off-device for cleanup
- Optional on-device AI explanations only where Apple Intelligence / Foundation Models are available
- No subscription, no always-on cleanup daemon required

## Build from source

Requires Xcode 18+ and XcodeGen.

```
gh repo clone AlexTkDev/MacOSCleaner
cd MacOSCleaner && xcodegen
open MacOSCleaner.xcodeproj
```

If macOS reports the app as damaged:

```
sudo xattr -r -c /path/to/MacOSCleaner.app
```

## FAQ (short)

- Free Mac cleaner? Yes, free to download for personal use via GitHub Releases.
- Replace macOS Storage? No — complements it.
- Cache cleaning safe? Safe categories are temporary; apps may rebuild caches. Review Moderate/Dangerous items; confirm before clean.
- Uninstaller-only? Yes — open Uninstaller, drop `.app`, review leftovers; full system scan not required.
- Docker/Xcode wipe projects? No — targets cache/tooling paths, not source repos; still review volumes/simulator data.
